## What he talks about most

Counted across the message (6,380 words; song blocks 44:25–46:51 left out): **God 53×**, **Lord 40×**, **saw 35×**, **Jesus 33×**, **glory 20×**, **year 19×**, **king 15×**, **throne 12×**, **victory 12×**, **robe 11×**, **grace 8×**.

The real count is a sentence: **"saw the Lord" 18 times**, **"I saw him" another 10**. One line of Isaiah 6:1, turned over until you have seen it.

## The one point he wants to make

**You can see the Lord — high, exalted, seated on the throne — in the very year that something in your life died. And because your guilt has been taken away by the finished work of Jesus, your answer can be: here am I, send me.**

> "it might be in a year that everything in my life has died but it's in that year that I saw the Lord" (04:41)

He hangs it on neither circumstances nor record: "God does not need everything to be perfect in your life in order to reveal himself to you" (03:31).

## The year something died

The recording opens inside this part: death, the kind that is not a funeral — a breakup, a divorce, "someone that swore they were going to have your back forever" (00:35). His own example: a youth pastor whose marriage was the picture of what he wanted, until he heard at university they had divorced.

> "you're my picture you're the one I'm looking to... and now you can't make it is there even hope for me" (02:17)

Then the verse with the year filled in: "in the year of the heartbreak" (02:48). A temporary king died, but Isaiah saw no shaken God: "I saw the Lord not scared... I saw the Lord not weak" (05:15).

## Seeing Him in the right picture

He says himself where the glory of Isaiah 6 points: "when Isaiah saw this he actually saw Jesus' glory" (06:57). Colossians 1:15 onwards is read out and applied to your church, family and body.

> "I wonder if we see him as the same Jesus that can work on a car. As the same Jesus that can transform a nation." (09:08)

Then Revelation 1:12 onwards in full. "When I saw him, it changed me" (11:04). He falls at his feet as though dead, and then the hand: "do not be afraid... I was dead and now look I am alive forever and ever" (12:54).

## You smell like what you sit in

The warmest part is a kitchen: his mother-in-law's fried chicken, and the smell still on your clothes when you leave.

> "I just sat in the room so long that it got on me... that want to smell like the glory of God" (16:22)

His diagnosis here is speed, not sin: "We're running from thing to thing to thing, but not sitting" (17:33). Two staff members had the worship team over with one rule — no phones; sit, worship, pray, nobody posts it (18:11). The way back is short: "All you have to do is repent again" (19:46).

## The train of His robe

Back to Isaiah 6:1, "the train of his robe filled the temple" (20:54). From the commentators: a king who won a battle cut a piece off the defeated king's garment onto his own robe, "to say I beat that king" (22:10).

> "his robe is so long because he has gone from victory after victory after victory after victory" (22:42)

Then the battle you are in now: "what makes you think that God can't do it now?" (23:16). His own marriage is one of those pieces of cloth — "it's a victory not that I won" (23:49).

## "Woe to me" — the coal, and "send me"

Isaiah's answer to the glory is not applause but "woe to me, I cried. I am ruined. I am a man of unclean lips" (27:10). Then a turn needing no word of knowledge: "I know in a room this size that in this room there is uncleanness" (28:23) — envy, grumbling, pride, unforgiveness. He never leaves it there; the seraph brings the coal.

> "Your guilt is taken away and your sin atoned for. Here is the grace of God on full display for me and for you." (30:43)

Only then the question, "whom shall I send and who will go for us" (32:28), and "Isaiah gives the only appropriate response Here am I Send me" (33:03). He illustrates it with his eleven-year-old's always-raised hand at the board.

> "here I am in my brokenness and in my weakness and in my shortcomings... I say here I am here I am Send me!" (36:23)

## The ministry time and the invitation

Two things are on his heart (36:23). First the death: "a year that something died" (37:03). Hands up, eyes closed, and "I'm not going to call you forward" (38:59) — then prayer: "Lord, you see your sons and your daughters with their hands up... they're your kids" (40:11).

Second, a call he is not sure what to do with: "this is not a salvation call this is a I'm all in call" (42:39) — no platform, no validation, "because God, you called me and that is enough" (43:14).

After the worship comes the call to Christ (47:25), for anyone whose heart is "not surrendered to the lordship and authority of Jesus Christ": "The Bible uses the word repent" (48:32). Everyone prays together:

> "Dear Jesus, I ask you to forgive me of all my sins... tonight I give you my heart I give you my life Give me the power to live for you in Jesus' name." (49:37)

## Scriptures for further reading

| Text | In the message | For further reading |
|---|---|---|
| Isaiah 6:1–8 | the throne, the robe, the coal, "send me" | verses 9–13 give the commission itself |
| 2 Chron. 26:16–21 | the king (02:48, 05:47) | not told here: "his pride led to his downfall" |
| John 12:41 | "he actually saw Jesus' glory" (06:57) | John quotes Isaiah 53:1 and 6:10 just before |
| Col. 1:15–18 | all things through him and for him | 19–20: peace "through his blood, shed on the cross" |
| Rev. 1:12–18 | the Son of Man; falling at his feet | verse 18: the keys of death and Hades; cf. Daniel 7 and 10 |
| Isaiah 6:3 · 6:6–7 | "completely holy God" (27:50); the coal (30:43) | the "Holy, holy, holy" is not in the recording; see Rev. 4:8 |
| Acts 3:19 | repent, "a turn" (48:32) | "turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out" |

**Grace first.** The order is not clean yourself up first. The seeing comes in a bad year; the uncleanness is named plainly and then dealt with by someone else: "by the finished work of the cross has made us right with God and it's not by our works but it's by grace through faith" (31:55). Only then comes "here am I" — and the sending is for the broken.

## From the rest of the session

- The recording **begins mid-message** (00:00), with no host introduction, and **stops just after the closing prayer** (50:09).
- **Testifying** (24:26–26:37): everyone shares one victory of the past year with the person next to them; that stretch transcribes as room noise. **Worship**, 44:25–47:20.
- **Referring back to the senior pastors** (37:45): "this is not just a conference. No, no, no, we're a family here. No masks."
- **Another pastor is invited up** before the dismissal (48:32); the recording has no speaker separation, so who leads it cannot be told.

## From the notebook

Notes taken during the message, checked against the transcript; what is not in the recording is marked.

- **"1 day — I saw the Lord"** — the refrain: "saw the Lord" 18 times (e.g. 04:41).
- *"Holy, holy, holy... the whole earth is full of his glory." — Isaiah 6:3* (the note writes *Isiah*) — **not in the recording**; what is there: "completely holy God" (27:50).
- *"He drifts in to pride he gets his eyes of god."* — **not found in the recording**; the king is named, but his story is not told here. Background: 2 Chron. 26:16.
- *"I saw the lord high / on throne no fear"* — "I saw the Lord high, exalted, and seated on the throne. I saw the Lord not scared." (05:15).
- *"Jesus is glory"* — "he actually saw Jesus' glory" (06:57).
- *"Agrarians chapter 1 / 15"* — the chapter read is **Colossians 1:15**; the note's word stands for Ephesians, which the speaker names himself (06:57).
- *"We going to see him high and exalted"* · *"Thing in heaven and"* — "We've got to see him high and exalted"; "things in heaven and on earth" (07:29).

> "it might be in a year that everything in my life has died but it's in that year that I saw the Lord" (04:41)
